learner_facing_text: A generic modular-deck course does not establish one universal assembly method, structural rating, guard/rail/stair requirement, inspection method, or acceptance authority. The actual system, manufacturer documentation, venue/AHJ requirements and responsible structural authority control those decisions.
notes: Model/manufacturer source is intentionally unresolved until a concrete system is selected for any practical build.

learner_facing_text: ANSI E1.21-2024 addresses temporary ground-supported structures used for technical production of outdoor entertainment events; it is not a universal standard for every indoor modular deck or platform system.
notes: Scope/version fact from ESTA index only; detailed structural requirements require the controlling standard text.

learner_facing_text: Entertainment structural systems are separated by system family in current standards; for example, aluminum trusses and towers are addressed separately from outdoor temporary ground-supported structures.
notes: Used to prevent cross-applying one structural standard to unrelated systems.

learner_facing_text: Before any model-specific practical staging lesson is released, the matrix must contain the exact manufacturer/model manual and the responsible practitioner/structural review for that system; generic standards are not enough.
notes: Internal release criterion created because the current course is generic and no controlling model manual is identified.

learner_facing_text: Staging leadership knowledge does not create structural-engineering, rigging, automation, manufacturer-acceptance, venue or AHJ authority; those decisions remain with the responsible external roles and controlling documents.
notes: Keeps lead responsibility separate from specialist authority.
